subject: Audit & access log handback scenarios — export formats, SLAs, and retention options
messages:
From: Hannah Jacobs <h.jacobs@finops-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: audit/access log retention + export for handback

Hi Sean,

Quick one from our side as we map out an on-prem migration: can you confirm the retention windows you offer for audit/access logs, and the exact export capabilities for customer handback? Specifically: 

- Default retention for audit and access logs (and whether that is configurable per-tenant).
- Supported export formats (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet, syslog streams, etc.).
- Typical lead time / SLA for a full historical extract (we have ~18 months of data).
- Options for direct SFTP/HTTPS delivery vs. downloadable archive.

We need these details for our compliance team (cc'd) as they prepare the evidence package. If you have a checklist or playbook you can attach, that would be super helpful.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Jacobs
Head of Compliance & Risk
FinOps Analytics
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Jacobs <h.jacobs@finops-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: audit/access log retention + export for handback

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Marissa is looping in on the technical export particulars. Attaching our handback checklist for quick reference.

- Retention (default): audit logs are retained for 180 days by default. Access logs (auth/console/API) are retained for 90 days by default. Both windows are configurable on Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted customers we can offer extended retention up to 3 years on a contractual basis (SLA + storage add-on).

- Export formats: we support NDJSON (recommended for event-level fidelity), compressed CSV (columnar-friendly for analytics teams), and Parquet (for large-scale analytics). We also support streaming syslog forwarding for ongoing ingestion during a handover period.

- Lead time / SLA: typical full-tenant historical extract (<= 1TB compressed) is delivered within 72 hours. Larger volumes are scoped case-by-case; we provide a project ETA as part of the export request and an electronic manifest. For on-prem handbacks we often schedule a phased export to reduce service impact.

- Delivery options: SFTP push (customer key), HTTPS download (pre-signed artifacts), or temporary cloud bucket handoff (customer-managed). Encrypted transfer (TLS + at-rest encryption) is standard.

See attached: handback-checklist.pdf — it contains the policies, minimum data schema, and an outline of the expected manifest. Marissa, can you add notes on our max throughput and an SFTP config example?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: handback-checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question: audit/access log retention + export for handback

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 09:05 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Marissa is looping in on the technical export particulars. Attaching our handback checklist for quick reference.

Hi Hannah — adding technical detail per request and a sample SFTP snippet. Key points: 

- Per-tenant configuration: For Dedicated and Private we can set retention policies per-tenant via the config API (retention_days: integer). Hosted accounts require a contractual change to increase beyond default retention.

- Export sizing & throughput: Our export pipeline uses parallel chunking. Baseline throughput for NDJSON exports is ~150 MB/min compressed (varies by window and compression). A ~1.2 TB compressed export will typically finish within 24–48 hours if we provision burst capacity. If you need a guaranteed 72-hour SLA for >2TB we include a dedicated export node (SLA add-on).

- Manifest & schema: Each export includes a top-level manifest.json (manifest contains filenames, start/end timestamps, compression, schema version). We will provide a sample manifest on request; below is an example line: 

  filename: logs_auth_2024-01-01_2026-10-28.ndjson.gz, events: 12,342,345, schema: v2.1

- Delivery/auth: SFTP delivery happens over FTPS or SFTP (your choice). We authenticate with a customer-managed SSH key; keys are rotated per the contract. For HTTPS delivery we produce pre-signed downloads and an integrity checksum (sha256).

- Deletion & verification: Post-export, we can schedule a secure wipe of the exported window (if requested) and issue a signed deletion certificate. Deletion from backups follows our normal retention policy unless you request a legal/contractual hold.

Attachments included: export-playbook.md (technical runbook), sftp-config-sample.txt (sample server block and recommended cipher list).

Let me know if you want a short call to review the manifest and the sample exports (we can spin up a test export of a single-week slice).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops Engineer — Observability
Redwood Inference
